## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Kilocode non-UTF-8 ripgrep matches SMALL ~2-3h (tools, grep, encoding)

- **What**: Kilocode PR #15056 (merged 2026-10-15) handles non-UTF-8 ripgrep matches in grep. Commit title: "fix(core): handle non-UTF-8 ripgrep matches in grep". Issue: repositories containing non-UTF-8 files (ISO-8859-1, Windows-1252, Latin-1) caused grep to fail with "Invalid ripgrep match output". Ripgrep's `--json` output emits `{"bytes": "<base64>"}` instead of `{"text": "..."}` when matched content is not valid UTF-8 (single Latin-1 byte like `0xF6` for `ö` triggers this). Grep parser only accepted `text` shape, so `bytes` records were rejected and whole search failed. Fix: (1) parser accepts both `text` and `bytes` shapes for matched line, file path, and submatches, (2) base64 bytes decoded as Windows-1252 (WHATWG mapping for ISO-8859-1, every byte maps to exactly one UTF-16 unit), (3) ripgrep byte offsets still line up with decoded text, message positions unchanged for UTF-8 files (never take bytes path).

- **Why**: Alexi has grep tool under `src/tool/tools/grep.ts` with ripgrep JSON parsing (L229-253 RgBeginEvent/RgMatchEvent interfaces, L437+ JSON streaming parser). Check if Alexi's grep parser handles `bytes` field in ripgrep JSON output or only `text`. Kilocode issue: files with Latin-1 encoding broke grep searches. Alexi equivalent: (1) audit `grep.ts` RgMatchEvent/RgBeginEvent interfaces for `bytes` field (L229-253), (2) check JSON parser for base64 decoding when `bytes` present (L437+ onData handler), (3) if only `text` accepted, add `bytes` fallback: (a) extend interfaces to include `bytes?: string` in path/lines/submatches, (b) decode base64 bytes as Windows-1252 (Node Buffer.from(base64, 'base64').toString('latin1')), (c) test with Latin-1 file (create file with `0xF6` byte, grep for pattern matching that byte, verify match returned not rejected). SMALL ~2-3h: audit grep.ts for bytes-field handling, add base64 decoding if missing, test Latin-1 file.

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/15056 (non-UTF-8 ripgrep matches), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/tool/tools/grep.ts L229-253 (RgMatchEvent interface), L437+ (JSON parser)

- **Category**: tools (grep, ripgrep, encoding, non-UTF-8)

- **Size**: SMALL ~2-3h (audit grep.ts for bytes-field handling in ripgrep JSON, add base64 Windows-1252 decoding if missing, test Latin-1 file match)

Check if Alexi honors `SAP_AI_GATEWAY_URL` or equivalent environment variable for gateway base URL override. Kilocode feature: custom gateway routing for proxies/regional endpoints. Alexi equivalent: (1) audit `src/providers/` for gateway base URL initialization (likely `https://api.ai.core.cloud.sap` or SAP-specific endpoint), (2) check if environment variable override exists (SAP_AI_GATEWAY_URL, ALEXI_GATEWAY_URL, AICORE_BASE_URL), (3) if no override, add SAP_AI_GATEWAY_URL support: (a) read `process.env.SAP_AI_GATEWAY_URL` at provider init, (b) validate URL (protocol, no path), (c) fallback to default SAP endpoint, (d) document in .env.example and PROVIDERS.md. #### 3. Cline plugin worker-only mode REFERENCE-ONLY ~4-6h (plugins, worker isolation)

- **What**: Cline PR #15069 (merged 2026-10-15) removes in-process plugin execution mode. Commit title: "feat(core): run plugins only in workers; drop the in-process mode". Change: `CLINE_PLUGIN_MODE` now supports only `worker` (default) or `sandbox`, `in_process` removed. Previously, plugins could run on host's main thread (in_process) or in worker threads (worker). In-process fallback (when no worker bootstrap available) turned silent plugin drops into silent in-host execution, hiding bootstrap-missing errors. New behavior: (1) plugins run ONLY in worker threads (one worker per plugin per session), (2) no worker bootstrap = PluginBootstrapMissingError (shows in `cline config tools`, `cline hub plugins`, session-start warnings), (3) worker crash (uncaught error, process.exit) turns off that plugin without killing host, (4) plugin registry loses in-process code (jiti import path, AsyncLocalStorage, __clinePluginHost shim), (5) tests covering retained behavior (hook timeouts, error modes, multi-session notices, capability checks) moved to worker suite. SSH remote helper (single-file upload, no bootstrap) now reports plugin tools missing instead of running in remote hub.

- **Why**: Alexi has plugin support under `src/plugin/` directory. Check if plugins run in-process or isolated (worker threads, child processes). Cline issue: in-process plugins could crash the host (uncaught error in plugin → whole extension reloads). Alexi equivalent: audit `src/plugin/index.ts` for plugin loading (import vs worker_threads.Worker vs child_process.fork), check if plugin failures are isolated (one plugin crash does not kill Alexi process). REFERENCE-ONLY: Cline worker-only pattern shows plugin isolation (worker per plugin, crash contained), loud bootstrap-missing errors (no silent fallback), and registry simplification (no in-process shim, no AsyncLocalStorage scoping). If Alexi plugins run in-process and users report plugin crashes killing the CLI, reference this pattern for worker-thread-only isolation ~4-6h (rewrite plugin loader, remove in-process fallback, add PluginBootstrapMissingError, test worker cleanup). Current priority UNKNOWN (depends on plugin crash frequency in Alexi, no evidence of in-process crashes yet). DEFER until crash reports arrive.

- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/15069 (plugin worker-only mode), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/plugin/ (Alexi plugin system)

- **Category**: N/A (plugins, worker isolation, reference-only)

- **Size**: SKIP immediate work. REFERENCE - audit Alexi plugin loading for isolation, reference Cline worker-only pattern if in-process plugins crash the host ~4-6h.

#### 4. Alexi glob/grep include-after-ignore SKIP (tools, glob, grep, already correct)

- **What**: Carry-forward from 2026-10-14 research #1 (Kilocode PR #15017 glob/grep include-after-ignore ordering). Alexi audit 2026-10-15: `src/tool/tools/grep.ts` L406-424 shows ignore globs are pushed to ripgrep args BEFORE include globs. Line 406 `args.push('--glob', '!node_modules', '--glob', '!dist', '--glob', '!build')` (hard-coded excludes), L407-413 push caller-supplied exclusion globs (`--glob=!${glob}`), L415-420 push allowlist globs (`--glob=${glob}`, no `!`), L422-423 push caller include (`--glob`, inc). Ripgrep evaluates `--glob` flags in order: excludes first (all `!` patterns), then includes (positive patterns), so include does NOT bypass earlier excludes - it can only opt specific ignored paths back in (intended allowlist behavior). Kilocode #15017 regression (include bypassing `.gitignore` via ripgrep `--glob` overrides) does NOT apply to Alexi - exclude ordering already correct. Yesterday's HIGH priority item #1 SKIP - no gap exists.

- **Why**: Yesterday's research (2026-10-14 #1) proposed auditing glob/grep tools for include-after-ignore ordering to prevent `.gitignore` bypass. Audit complete 2026-10-15: Alexi already implements correct ordering (excludes before includes in ripgrep args). SKIP - no gap exists.

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/15017 (glob/grep include-after-ignore), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/tool/tools/grep.ts L406-424 (exclude-before-include ordering verified)

- **Category**: N/A (tools, glob, grep, already correct)

- **Size**: SKIP. Alexi already implements correct include-after-ignore ordering in grep.ts. Verified 2026-10-15.

#### 5. Kilocode fork-from-message MEDIUM ~4-6h (command, session)

- **What**: Carry-forward from 2026-10-14 research #2 (Kilocode PR #15004 fork-from-message). Alexi audit 2026-10-15: `src/cli/interactive.ts` L803-841 implements `/fork` command. Line 809 `const forkName = args[0] || 'fork-${Date.now()}'` takes optional fork name from args. Line 830 `const newSession = await sessionManager.createSession(session.workdir, session.provider, session.model, session.messages)` creates new session with `session.messages` (entire message history copied, no truncation). Line 832-841 sets fork title and switches to forked session. **No from-message support exists** - fork always copies entire session history from start. Kilocode #15004 feature (fork starting at chosen message id, truncating history at that point) is a gap. Use case: user wants to branch from specific point in long conversation (e.g. after message 10 of 30), exploring alternative path without carrying later messages.

- **Why**: Yesterday's research (2026-10-14 #2) proposed auditing fork implementation for from-message support. Audit complete 2026-10-15: Alexi has `/fork` command but only full-session fork (all messages copied), no from-message truncation. Gap exists. Implementation: (1) add `--from-message <message_id>` flag to `/fork` command (parse args after fork name), (2) modify fork logic to copy session up to specified message (slice `session.messages` at message index), (3) validate message id exists in source session (error if not found), (4) test forking from mid-conversation (create session with 10 messages, fork from message 5, verify forked session has only messages 1-5). MEDIUM ~4-6h: add from-message parameter to fork command, implement transcript truncation at fork point, test mid-conversation fork.

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/15004 (fork-from-message), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/cli/interactive.ts L803-841 (fork command verified, no from-message support)

#### 8. Cline OpenAI Compatible base URL path REFERENCE-ONLY (vscode, providers)

- **What**: Cline PR #15057 (merged 2026-10-15) stops appending default `/v1` path to OpenAI Compatible base URLs. Commit title: "fix(vscode): don't append default path to OpenAI Compatible base URL". Issue: SDK client inherited default path `/v1` for URLs with no path, turning `https://abc.com` into `https://abc.com/v1`. OpenAI Compatible endpoints are user-supplied and were passed verbatim by legacy client. Fix: skip default-path inheritance for OpenAI Compatible provider (user-supplied URLs used as-is).
